note: The bzip2 format written from its specification as Forge's own primitive (no library): Burrows-Wheeler transform by prefix doubling, move-to-front with zero runs, up to six Huffman tables with code lengths of at most 17, the bzip2 CRC-32. Block size (100s of kb) is block-size, 1 to 9, default 9 (else E_RANGE). Work factor is accepted (0 to 250, default 30, else E_RANGE) and ignored: it only tunes libbzip2's choice between two sorting algorithms, and Forge has one. The empty input gives the valid 14-byte empty stream instead of CyberChef's 'Please provide an input' error. The bytes can differ from libbzip2's (the Huffman refinement is not identical) except for tiny or very regular inputs, and bzip2, Python and libbzip2 read them.

The bzip2 format written from its specification (inverse BWT, MTF, Huffman, run-length step, randomised blocks, block and stream CRC-32). Several streams one after the other are joined, as bzip2 -d does; bytes after the last stream that do not start another are ignored. Added: verify, on by default, checks every CRC (E_COERCE otherwise); off, a bad checksum is ignored. CyberChef's low-memory option (use a slower algorithm in libbzip2) has no meaning here and is not offered. Corrupt or cut-short data is E_COERCE naming the fault; a block larger than its header's block size allows is E_COERCE; output past the value limit (16 MiB for shared recipes, 64 MiB otherwise) stops with E_LIMIT_VALUE while decoding. CyberChef also rejects an empty input; here an empty input is E_COERCE as not bzip2 data.
